# okbase

> okbase makes a folder of markdown knowledge (an Open Knowledge Format bundle, a docs site, a wiki, an Obsidian vault) easy for AI agents to use: an MCP server and CLI with multilingual search (measured on Vietnamese, English and Japanese), metadata queries, SQL over spreadsheets, optional semantic search and fine-tuning, and Agent Skills for Claude Code and Codex. Rust, MIT OR Apache-2.0, read-only by default, no telemetry.

Users paste a prompt to their agent; the agent sets okbase up and the user only answers questions. The procedure:

1. Install if `okbase --version` fails: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tidusvn05/okbase/main/install.sh | sh` (add `-s -- --full` for semantic search and fine-tuning; Windows: `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tidusvn05/okbase/main/install.ps1 | iex`). If you cannot run it (no network, a sandbox, no write access to ~/.local/bin), give the user the command and wait. Before the first release the installer finds no release; install from source instead (Rust 1.89+, a few minutes): `cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/tidusvn05/okbase okbase-cli`.
2. Run `okbase onboard` in the knowledge folder (`--json` for structured output; `--goal curate` to improve a bundle, `--goal remove` to remove okbase). It inspects the folder (docs site, repository with `docs/`, empty folder) and plans every step. Do the first step, run `okbase onboard` again, repeat until no steps are left.
3. `run` steps: run them. `ask` steps: ask the user the question verbatim and wait; run only the commands of the option they chose (a step they declined stays listed: treat it as done). `tell` steps: tell the user (for example, inside Codex the user connects Codex: `okbase agent install --codex` in their own terminal).
4. Never add `--accept-license`, `--yes`, `--write`, `--force`, `--replace` or `--send-documents` unless the user agreed. A command that exits 3 needs the user: relay its `error.question` (or, for `sandbox_blocked`, its `next` command). Exit 4 means findings (lint errors, a rejected batch, a failed gate).
5. Finish with `okbase doctor` (a real MCP round trip). Then report in a few lines, in the user's language: what is set up (`done`), how to use it now (`report.use_now`, usually: restart the agent session once), and the optional upgrades (`report.optional`), which you do only if asked.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): what okbase does, builds, fine-tuning
- [Usage](docs/usage.md): small, medium and large projects; every scenario (several bundles, several projects, shared servers, removing okbase)
- `okbase help --agent`: the agent contract (JSON, exit codes, error codes, consent rules, commands)
- `okbase embed tune guide`: fine-tuning the search model with agent-written questions

- [Design](docs/design.md): architecture and the evidence behind every default
